newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence 116.8 in Jan vs rvsd 114.2.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence 116.8 in Jan vs rvsd 114.2.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence jumped to 116.8 in January, up from a revised reading of 114.2 in December, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
"Consumer confidence reached a new high for the decade in the first month of 1997," the report said.

The present situation component rose more than four points to 139.8 -- "a seven -and-a-half-year high," the conference board said. The expectations component of the January index advanced to 101.5, up slightly from a revised 99.9 reading in the previous month, it said.
"The rising tide of consumer optimism that was characteristic of 1996 has spilled into 1997," said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Conference Board's Consumer Research Center.

"Consumer confidence is at an all-time high for the 1990s, and overall economic conditions remain positive, suggesting that 1997 will be yet another year of economic expansion," she said. (( -- N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1660 ))
